title: Internal readiness scripts, SDK warnings, and customer upgrade sprints
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Goal: deliver a cross-functional execution kit that reduces customer upgrade friction during the upcoming API/contract sunset. The kit includes: 1) internal readiness scripts and checklists for Support/SE/Success, 2) SDK runtime deprecation warnings and automated changelog notices, 3) a segmented comms calendar and canary upgrade cohorts, and 4) a small set of programmatic migration helpers (Python/Node) for the most common breaking changes.

Scope & deliverables:
- Release note templates: concise user-facing bullets + expanded migration steps, FAQ, and rollback instructions. (Target: one short note + one deep-dive per release).
- SDK changes: add runtime WARN logs for deprecated endpoints, bump minor semver across SDKs with in-build deprecation messaging and links to migration docs. Reference repos: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python and sdk-js.
- Internal readiness scripts: runnable playbooks (bash/python) that pull customer usage by endpoint, generate upgrade risk buckets, and produce a prioritized outreach list for Success.
- Support/SE enablement: 3x 45-minute internal workshops, updated KB articles, and templated playbooks for escalation.
- Customer migration sprint: pilot with 15 high-usage customers (selected by risk bucket), weekly checkpoints, and automated progress dashboard.

Key decisions so far:
- We will ship SDK deprecation warnings in SDK minor releases rather than relying solely on email comms (Decision made 2026-02-26).
- Canary cohort uses region + usage-profile segmentation (latency-sensitive, high-throughput, embeddings-only).
- We will not require a security review for the migration helpers; they are read-only and advisory.

Monitoring & success metrics:
- 80% of pilot customers complete migration within 21 days of first outreach.
- Reduction in support tickets for the deprecated endpoint by 60% two weeks after general availability.
- SDK download + migration guide click-through tracked via UTM links and a lightweight dashboard (console-2026.04/dashboards/migration-progress).

Artifacts & links:
- Draft release notes + templates: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/PM-70321-release-notes-templates
- Migration helpers repo (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/migration-kits/pull/12
- SDK runtime PR (warnings): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/498
- Internal KB (Support): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3pm-support-playbooks
- Pilot signup sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1pilot-signups
- Slack channel: #release-runway (ongoing coordination)

Open risks & mitigations:
- Risk: customers using obscure parameter combos could break migration scripts. Mitigation: include a fallthrough compatibility shim and a 'dry-run' mode in helpers.
- Risk: SDK release cadence slower than needed. Mitigation: allocate a small hotfix window for each SDK (ENG-88421).
- Risk: Support capacity spikes during rollout. Mitigation: temporary rotations and playbook runbooks drafted; plan to onboard 2 contractors if needed.
